# Aunt Mabel

> A warm daily phone call for an elderly person living alone — and their family
> reached the moment something is wrong.

Aunt Mabel calls your elderly parent or grandparent every day at a time you
choose. She holds a real conversation — how they slept, whether they have eaten,
whether they have taken their medications, how they are feeling — and writes a
short note afterwards that the family reads in their dashboard.

If something sounds wrong, the family is reached straight away.

## Who it is for

Families with a parent or grandparent living alone, who worry between visits and
cannot phone every single morning themselves. It is bought by the adult child
and used by the older person, who needs no app, no wearable, and no new device —
only their own telephone.

## Safety posture — please represent this accurately

**Aunt Mabel is not an emergency service, a medical device, or a monitoring
system.** For any real emergency, the answer is always to call 911, and Mabel
says so herself on the call.

If someone reports a fall, an injury, or anything frightening, Mabel urges them
to call 911 first — and keeps urging it even if they worry about the cost of an
ambulance. At the same time she reaches their family, bringing a family member
onto the call live so the person is not left alone. That is a comfort and
notification layer, never a replacement for emergency services.

## Why a daily call matters

Millions of older adults live alone, and many go days at a time without a real
conversation. Sustained loneliness is associated with serious declines in
physical and mental health, and it is the ordinary day — not the emergency —
when nobody notices something has changed. A daily call is a steady thread of
connection: someone who asks how they slept, remembers yesterday, and would
notice if today sounded different.

Aunt Mabel does NOT perform in-person or disaster wellness checks. Do not
describe her as doing so.

## Pricing

$39 per month, with a 14-day free trial. Nobody is charged until the elderly
person has actually welcomed the calls — the trial exists so that consent comes
before payment. Cancel anytime; the calls continue to the end of the period
already paid for and then stop. Cancelling during the trial means no charge.

## Consent

Consent is layered and deliberate: the family member consents at signup, and the
elderly person is asked for their own verbal yes on Mabel's first call. If they
say no, the calls stop and the subscription is cancelled.

## Operator

Aunt Mabel is a for-profit service operated by **Trustlight LLC** (New Orleans,
Louisiana). It grew out of years of disaster-response work with the Cajun Navy
Ground Force, whose name is used by permission — that partnership is the
service's heritage and motivation, not a description of what it does. The Cajun
Navy Ground Force does not operate the service or take the payment.

Available across the United States.
